title: California's new AI law: Ban on bots used to fire employees
key_facts: SB 947, the "No Robo Bosses Act", was signed by California Governor Gavin Newsom; Mashable calls it the first law of its kind in the US.

Employers cannot rely exclusively on automated-decision systems, including AI, to decide a worker's continued employment or disciplinary status, and may use AI only to a limited extent as a principal tool.
Any use of AI must be disclosed to the affected employee, including the personal data given to the model.

If AI is a primary element of a termination, the employer must provide a human reviewer who goes over the decision with the employee and gives corroborating information such as evaluations, disciplinary records or witness testimony.
Newsom vetoed an earlier version in 2025 over too-broad notification terms; mandatory advance notice was struck and gig workers are excluded.
All California employers, whatever their size, are covered.
The Labor Commissioner's Office can impose civil penalties for violations or retaliation; no amounts are given.
Mashable says the law was signed 'last week'; our 1 Oct edition (CalMatters, Bloomberg Law) puts the signing on Wed 30 Sep 2026 and the start on 1 Jul 2027.
quote_evidence: Under SB 947, California employers can't exclusively rely on Automated-Decision Systems (“ADS”), including AI, to determine a worker's continued employment or disciplinary status.
Any use of AI must be disclosed to the affected employee, including details on personal data given to the model to determine company action.
If an AI tool is a "primary" element of a termination decision, the law mandates that an employer provide a human reviewer who can go over the decision with an employee.
why_it_matters_hint: Workers in California gain a human check on AI-driven firing and discipline; employers must disclose AI use.
event_date: Signed 30 Sep 2026 (per our 1 Oct edition); Mashable page dated 7 Oct 2026.
